column1: # T-GATES-047 timing-bound test list: every #[test] function whose verdict the scan ties to the real clock. Three shapes:
# (1) its own body waits (sleep, sleep_ms, recv_timeout, wait_timeout, wait_timeout_ms, wait_timeout_while, park_timeout, park_timeout_ms: stable std) or measures (elapsed);
# (2) its own body does clock arithmetic between two different Instant::now()/SystemTime::now() readings (T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS);
# (3) it reaches, through resolved call-graph edges, a test-only helper of its target that keeps a measurement (T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS).
# bt-source's timing test holds the tree to this list both ways; scripts/ci/check-timing-bound.ps1 lets whole
# rows only disappear against the merge base, except for the rows a new widening line admits by count. A real-time window in
# product code is not seen by the scan: a product function's own Instant::now()/SystemTime::now()/elapsed() deadline or bound,
# its own std wait (recv_timeout, wait_timeout*, park_timeout*) on a Duration read from no clock, or a Duration a test hands to
# a product wait. The walk ends at the first product function, and that a test reaches a product clock decides nothing about
# whether another thread acts inside its window. Plan row 125 swept bt-app and bt-platform by hand on 2026-10-31 at 9ac40b223,
# and plan row 153 swept the std waits on 2026-11-01 at 417b32f65 (their `# noted` lines below); review owns any window added
# since. A `# noted` line records such a clock found and closed by review: it moves no row.
# widened 2026-10-24 by T-TIMING-BOUND-STRAYS (+20 rows): clock arithmetic in a test's own body, a budget measured in a test-only helper

# shrunk 2026-10-27 by T-TRIAL-DEATH-WAIT-CONTROLLED-CLOCK (-4 rows): the trial watch's "dies, ends the wait at once" tests, both platforms, count the pauses of the road's update_apply::TrialClock instead of timing the road

# shrunk 2026-10-27 by T-ELAPSED-UPPER-BOUNDS-ON-OTHER-WAITS (-4 rows): O's wait for its applier counts the pauses of update_apply::WaitClock; the panic road's and the claims' "never waits for a held lock" are a signal awaited within the suite's patience; the live applier at Handoff has no wait to time and is proven by the state it leaves

# shrunk 2026-10-29 by T-ELAPSED-BOUNDS-ON-FLOODS-AND-TRACE-SINK (-7 rows): the hand-off lane's flood, the trace sink's producers, its writer past a held stderr lock and its shutdown are each a signal awaited while the holder is still held, within the suite's patience, with the holder let go before the verdict

# shrunk 2026-10-30 by T-LANE-CONTRACT-PROMPT-BOUND (-14 rows): the lane contract's full-queue claim proves "the flood returned while the executor was still held" by the gate's count of the times it let go on its own, not by timing each submission against 1 s; no claim helper keeps a measurement, and a lapse in any claim is red

# shrunk 2026-10-30 by T-TESTS-WHOSE-RED-IS-A-HANG (-1 rows): the watchdog's report past a held stderr lock, and its "one more" offer to the stalled sink, are each a signal awaited while the holder is still held, within the suite's patience, with the holder let go before the verdict

# not seen 2026-10-31 by T-FLOATING-VIDEO-DOUBLE-CLICK-TIMING (no row changes): eight picture, recording and page tests whose double click was decided by the product's multi-click counters on the wall clock (a clock reached through a product function, the blind spot above) now count their presses on the window's held PointerClock; a scan for such product windows is plan row 125's

# shrunk 2026-10-31 by T-UPDATE-APPLIER-LOCK-WAITS (-4 rows): the applier's wait for O's lock is reached as state (its election over), the claim and O itself are let go in the pause of the road's first refused ask on its watched update_apply::WaitClock, and every give-up behind a hold the test keeps is awaited while it is still held, within the suite's patience

# noted 2026-10-31 by T-UPDATE-APPLY-FLIP-HOLD-FLAKE (0 rows): the update applier's wait for a live trial's final decision after the commit, and its held moves' window, are read and paused on the road's update_apply::WaitClock (Road::decision_clock on both platforms, Road::held_clock on Windows; WallClock in the product); the harnesses' decision clock lets its first pause last until the trial's receipt is gone, within the suite's patience, and the held-moment tests count the window's pauses: a real-time window in a product function that a test thread raced, unlisted because no scan of test bodies sees it (plan row 125)

# noted 2026-10-31 by T-LANE-DOOR-CALLS-ON-THE-TEST-THREAD (0 rows): the 33 lane-door tests whose fake's work stands in a lane::Hold, and the lanes' module tests held at the suite's Gate, are red by the holder's count of the times it let go on its own at the suite's patience, read at its release, not by a clock; Hold::pass keeps no measurement and its cap only ends in a red; the taskbar reading made while the shell is held is a signal awaited within the suite's patience, with the shell let go before the verdict

# noted 2026-10-31 by T-DIAGNOSTICS-TWO-PRODUCERS-WALL-BUDGET (0 rows): the diagnostics log's two-producer test waited 30 s on the writer's settle (Queue::settle's recv_timeout, a product function) for 40,000 lines and a loaded machine ran out of it; it now waits for the queue's close while the writer's count of lines still to take falls (lane::while_progressing), and the module's other settles that must be written are awaited within the suite's patience by name: a clock reached through a product function, the blind spot above (plan row 125)

# shrunk 2026-10-31 by T-TIMING-CENSUS-PRODUCT-WINDOWS (-2 rows): O's wait for the applier it started, in the Windows applier tests, is read and paused on update_apply::CountedClock (old_leaves_on): the applier's mark ends it inside the pause the test chooses, and a silent applier's budget is the clock's count, not a sleep or an elapsed reading

# noted 2026-10-31 by T-TIMING-CENSUS-PRODUCT-WINDOWS (0 rows): plan row 125's hand sweep of bt-app and bt-platform at 9ac40b223 judged the 60 product functions that hold its 95 window-shaped Instant/SystemTime/elapsed reads (66 verdicts once same-named functions are split and write_journal is added) and 13 test sites that hand a wall-clock bound to a product wait; 26 functions and one recv_timeout window are gaps another thread or process must meet inside real time, now plan rows 136-153 (T-TRIAL-STOP-QUIT-GRACE-ON-THE-ROAD-CLOCK to T-FIRST-FRAME-BUDGET-FROM-A-CLOCK: each wait read on a clock seam; a 19th, the diagnostics tests' settle bound, was closed by T-DIAGNOSTICS-TWO-PRODUCERS-WALL-BUDGET); the rest are timeouts the tests outlast, decide by state, or never reach; the 475 plain timestamps (readings handed down as now, recorded or logged) were left out; O's end in every Windows and macOS applier test now waits on a CountedClock

# shrunk 2026-11-01 by T-STALE-MARK-RACE-ON-A-COUNTED-CLOCK (-1 rows): a contender's wait for the election lock a test holds is read and paused on update_apply::CountedClock (update_apply::take_the_window_on, through install_txn::hold_by); its first pause tells the test it waits and lasts until the test has written the live owner and let the lock go, so no sleep of the test's is raced against the 5 s election window

# noted 2026-11-01 by T-STALE-MARK-RACE-ON-A-COUNTED-CLOCK (0 rows): plan row 125's G2 (take_the_window_within_using) is closed: in the stale-mark race both racers' election-lock waits are read and paused on one CountedClock of the round (install_txn::hold_by), whose first pause lasts until the other racer has answered, and the round asserts at most one pause; the mark-write and read retries (JOURNAL_WRITE_WITHIN) are never spent there, since a contender with no worker asks each once (the census's "5 s against 2 s" was 5 s against one unpaused read-read-write)

# shrunk 2026-11-01 by T-LAUNCH-HANDOVER-BUDGET-ON-A-CLOCK (-5 rows): the launch wire's waits for the other end on both platforms (the second launch's budget: the reply on Windows, every frame on Unix; the server's step deadline; the Windows listener's first word) are read on a launch_conversation::LaunchClock (RealClock in the product, through hand_over and LaunchPipe::start), and the Windows busy retry's own waits are counted through LaunchClock::spent; the Windows writes stay on write_bounded's real 250 ms (noted below), and the launch_pipe tests hand a CountedClock: the other end's answer is awaited within the door suites' patience, a spent budget or step is the clock's count, and a refused line's or an unconfirmed launch's absence is read as state (the next launch's commit is the first)

# noted 2026-11-01 by T-LAUNCH-HANDOVER-BUDGET-ON-A-CLOCK (0 rows): the Windows write_bounded deadline (attention_pipe, 250 ms) stays on the real clock, decided by buffering (every frame fits the pipe's quota) and not by the peer; the bt-app tests that cross the real endpoint (launch_wire::tests::a_carried_start_reaches_the_folio_that_holds_the_data_directory, retried by carry_the_start for ACKNOWLEDGED_WITHIN, and the three two-copies tests, two real processes) stay on the product's real clock, which no counted clock can reach across a process without a product knob; the fixed-millisecond kernel waits outside row 125's grammar (attention_pipe and the rest of bt-platform) are plan row 163

# noted 2026-11-01 by T-APPLIER-HOLD-CAP-UNDER-LOAD (0 rows): p_waits_for_o_and_releases_the_claim, both platforms, awaited P's whole commit after O let go of its lock within one suite's patience on the wall clock (ended_while_held with nothing held), around durable journal writes, write-through moves, a trial process and the decision clock's own patience, and a loaded machine ran out of it; it now awaits the commit while the steps the disk shows fall (update_apply::commit_steps_left, lane::while_progressing), and every *_while_held helper names its caller: a clock reached through product functions, the blind spot above; the applier's remaining real-time lock and election waits are plan rows 138 and 146

# shrunk 2026-11-01 by T-TRIAL-STOP-QUIT-GRACE-ON-THE-ROAD-CLOCK (-2 rows): the trial stop's quit grace and end window (update_apply::stop_trial) are read and paused on the road's Road::stop_clock (an update_apply::WaitClock, both platforms); the two tests that pinned the grace by real time count it on update_apply::CountedClock::stopping, the end awaited as the ended trial's own state, and the macOS one's ready and stranger waits are awaited as state

# noted 2026-11-01 by T-TRIAL-STOP-QUIT-GRACE-ON-THE-ROAD-CLOCK (0 rows): a_receipt_for_another_nonce_is_refused and five more macOS tests that stop a live trial (G1 of plan row 125, 1 s of real time) hold the stop clock's first pause until their waiter has reaped the trial, so ended within the grace is state at a counted pause; the Windows tests that run a silent trial through a rollback keep WallClock (600 ms grace, a lower bound, then a 10 s end window)

# noted 2026-11-01 by T-DIR-WATCH-RETIRE-DOORS-ON-A-CLOCK (0 rows): the directory-watch tests on both platforms asserted that a watcher left within DIR_WATCH_RETIRE_BUDGET (2 s, the bound DirWatch::retire_within and DirWatchSet::retire_within poll to, product functions) by handing the product's own budget to the door; their helpers now hand the door the suite's patience, so the watcher's leaving is the state awaited, and await the door's answer on a worker within its bound and the patience after it, so a budget that never ends is a named red: a clock reached through a product function, the blind spot above (plan rows 125 G15, 149)
